review_notes: I read the whole target file and the related Frames.lean definitions (restrictSection, restrictFrame, coefficient_restrict). I grepped the Seshadri tree for an existing lemma stating how restrictSection interacts with post-composition and found none. restrictSection_comp concerns composing the open immersions, not post-composing the section. The same restriction-functoriality reasoning appears in three proofs: two in the target and one in Frames.lean. The other similar-looking pattern is the Associated.trans, change-of-frame, unit-factor ending of affineCoefficient_power and affineCoefficient_sectionMultiply. I did not report it because the unit-factor lemmas differ and the shared part is short. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma and the rewritten uses are untested sketches. Also, each repeated block is routine category-theoretic bookkeeping, so the finding's strength rests on it being repeated three times.

findings.problem: The proof re-derives, as a local 10-line calc, that restricting a section commutes with post-composition. That is restrictSection φ (s ≫ a) = restrictSection φ s ≫ (restrictFunctor φ).map a, which is functoriality of restrictFunctor plus associativity. affineCoefficient_sectionMultiply proves the same identity again as `restrictedComposition` (lines 84-87). Frames.lean's coefficient_restrict proves it a third time with an identical calc. There is no named lemma for this identity, so each proof unfolds restrictSection by hand and introduces the `restriction` and `unitIso` lets to do so.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to restrictSection in Frames.lean: `lemma restrictSection_comp_hom (φ : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion φ] {M N : X.Modules} (s : O X ⟶ M) (a : M ⟶ N) : restrictSection φ (s ≫ a) = restrictSection φ s ≫ (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor φ).map a := by unfold restrictSection; rw [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]`. In affineCoefficient_iso, rewrite the `composition`/`equality` steps as `coefficient (restriction.mapIso g ≪≫ f) (restrictSection U.1.ι s) = coefficient f (restrictSection U.1.ι (s ≫ g.hom))` by unfolding `coefficient`, using `Category.assoc` and `← restrictSection_comp_hom`, then apply `congrArg U.1.topIso.hom`. In affineCoefficient_sectionMultiply, replace `restrictedComposition` by `restrictSection_comp_hom U.1.ι t multiplication`. In Frames.lean's coefficient_restrict, replace `composition` the same way before applying endValue_restrict. The lemma needs no new imports, because the target already imports the Sheaves files and Frames.lean is upstream of them.
findings.benefit: This removes three copies of the same fragile calc and the `let restriction`/`let unitIso` scaffolding. Each use shrinks to one rewrite. The identity gets a discoverable name, so later coefficient lemmas that restrict composed sections can reuse it instead of redoing the associativity bookkeeping.

evidence.excerpt:
_ = unitIso.inv ≫ restriction.map (s ≫ e.hom) ≫ unitIso.hom :=
        congrArg (fun morphism => unitIso.inv ≫ morphism ≫ unitIso.hom)
          (restriction.map_comp s e.hom).symm
